text: SEC EDGAR enforces its fair-access policy: a User-Agent carrying a repo URL gets a flat 403, the same request with a contact email returns 200. EDGAR is therefore gated on settings.sec_enabled() (STOCKY_SEC_CONTACT) and skips itself when unset.

Bing News RSS answers a multi-term OR query with an EMPTY feed where Google News returns a full one. Bing needs a single quoted phrase plus 'stock' (services/news/bing_news.build_query); it cannot share google_news.build_query.

GDELT rejected as a news source: phrase search too loose ("shell" returns awards shows and retirement advice), legal suffix absent from body copy so the precise form finds nothing, ~20s TLS handshake and 429 at 1 req/5s. Cost more latency than all other sources combined for articles the relevance filter dropped. Bing covers the non-US reach instead.

Nasdaq's per-ticker RSS (www.nasdaq.com/feed/rssoutbound?symbol=X) returns GENERIC market news for unknown symbols rather than an empty feed - same trap as Yahoo's symbol-keyed endpoints. Keep NASDAQ out of dedup._RELATED_ALLOWED.

Nasdaq quote API splits a quote into primaryData (trading now, extended hours after the bell) and secondaryData (regular close). Use the regular-session block whenever present, else an after-hours print gets stored as the day's close. Also refuse suffixed symbols - SHEL.L would return the NY ADR.

Killing the uvicorn reloader on Windows can orphan its listening socket: main.py runs reload=True and the reloader binds with SO_REUSEADDR, so after a hard kill the socket outlives its PID and a new server binds port 5000 alongside it. Windows then splits connections between the zombie and the new process and the zombie answers with the code it started with, so an edit appears to take effect on some requests only. Detect with netstat -ano | grep ':5000 .*LISTENING' - more than one row is a zombie, and Get-Process on that PID says the process does not exist. Start on a different port to work around it.

Only about 5% of stored articles carry an image: most arrive via a Google News redirect, which services/news/images.py skips because resolving one costs a request and rarely yields an og:image, and STOCKY_IMAGE_FETCH_LIMIT caps fetches at 12 per stock per refresh. Any UI that leads with a picture must pick the first article that has one rather than the top-ranked article, or the hero slot is empty most of the time.

News feed diversity is not enforced server-side. marketbeat.com posts a near-identical 'X acquires N shares of NVIDIA' filing story every few minutes, so ORDER BY publish_time DESC returns ten of them in a row. The frontend caps per-source and per-symbol counts when rendering its recency column; if a second wire starts doing the same under rotating domains the fix belongs in services/dedup.py, not the client.
